text:
The Nifty 50 closed at 25,514.3, up 1.14% on the day, while the broader Nifty 500 rose 1.13%. Gains were wide‑based: 350 stocks advanced versus 143 declines, giving a breadth score of 71.9 (healthy). All major sectors in the “leading” quadrant – PSU banks, private banks, financial services, auto and FMCG – posted strength, while lagging groups such as pharma, IT and mid‑caps lagged. The India VIX stayed low at 15.57, indicating modest volatility.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were net buyers of about ₹7,411 crore, extending a 16‑day buying streak, while Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold roughly ₹1,357 crore. In futures, FIIs were net short about 68,247 contracts but added 2,423 contracts versus the prior session. Options data show a put‑call ratio (PCR) of 1.47 for Nifty and 1.36 for Bank Nifty, suggesting more put interest. The “max‑pain” levels are 25,300 for Nifty and 61,000 for Bank Nifty, with call walls at 26,000 and 64,000 and put walls at 25,000 and 61,000 respectively.

Watch the 25,378 pivot (P) and the 25,241 support (S1) on the Nifty; a break below S1 could test the 24,996 dma200. For Bank Nifty, the pivot is 62,692 and support 62,322; a slip under support may target the 56,725 dma200. Key headlines to monitor include global AI‑related sell‑offs, oil price moves after Houthi attacks, and any CPI data hinting at inflation above 6% that could affect RBI policy. These factors could shape the next session’s direction.
